world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Read Fabre 2005 (Los enlhet-enenlhet, ling.fi PDF) and Brid 2023 'Procesos de lexicalización en angaité' (full PDF): neither contains any stress/acento statement; no grammar or phonology of Angaité exists.

new_statements.quote: Prosody also presents some evidence for the relevance of the syllable. Stress is primarily word-final, with the exception of some affixes that seem not to take stress (or perhaps other morphology attracts it). This impressionistic analysis of stress placement, based on my perception of the stressed syllable in each unit, would benefit from a systematic investigation of the acoustic correlates of stress. At the moment, however, it appears that word-level prominence targets syllables, regardless of how exactly that prominence is realized.

Stress is primarily word-final, with the exception of some affixes that seem not to take stress (or perhaps othe…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary word stress falls on the final syllable of the word; the exceptions are certain affixes that do not take stress (so that stress stays on the base or is attracted by other morphology). The author flags the analysis as impressionistic (auditory), pending acoustic study. Supporting remarks elsewhere in the same report: pitch tends to rise in the final syllable of bisyllabic words (p. 61; n. 9 p. 51: second vowel higher-pitched by 20-80 Hz in maek, yaayet, yaamet); some vowels are much longer than others, often the penultimate vowel (p. 72), length 'often seeming to appear before an apparently stressed syllable' (p. 81).
new_statements.exceptions: Some affixes seem not to take stress, or other morphology attracts it (p. 57); interaction of stress with affixation in verbs is left for future work (p. 3, p. 81); stress, pitch and phonation are not marked in the transcriptions (p. 7).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level, from elicited word lists and simple sentences (18 h of semi-structured elicitation with two speakers from La Leona, La Patria, July 2019); the author explicitly calls the stress statement impressionistic and calls for acoustic verification; the report is about consonants and syllables, and stress is discussed only as evidence for the syllable.
new_statements.identity_note: The statement describes the Angaité of La Patria (Presidente Hayes), specifically speakers from the La Leona village (data July 2019), i.e. the language-level variety anga1316; no separate dialect glottocode. Note that IDS lists the Sammons wordlist as "Sanapaná (Angaité dialect)" under anga1316, and Brid 2023 miscites Wheeler 2020 as a doctoral thesis (it is an M.A. Report).
